title: Homotopy invariance of simplicial maps into a Kan complex
statement:
Use simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets, Kan complexes, geometric realization and weak homotopy equivalences as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $u:A\to B$ be a map of small simplicial sets whose geometric realization induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups, and let $Z$ be a Kan complex in a universe containing $A$ and $B$. Then $\operatorname{Fun}(A,Z)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(B,Z)$ are Kan complexes, and precomposition induces a simplicial homotopy equivalence
$$u^*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,Z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(A,Z).$$
Here simplicial homotopy equivalence means that a simplicial map in the opposite direction exists with both composites simplicially homotopic to the respective identities; a simplicial homotopy from $f_0:X\to Y$ to $f_1:X\to Y$ is a map $X\times\Delta^1\to Y$ with those two endpoint restrictions. In particular $u^*$ induces a bijection on connected components, where components are vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges. No Kan condition on $A$ or $B$, no nonemptiness condition, and no monomorphism condition on $u$ is imposed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.1.7.17, Tag 03PJ; Corollary 3.1.3.4, Tag 00TN, for the Kan condition, and Corollary 3.6.4.3, Tag 03X7, to pass from the geometric-realization definition to Definition 3.1.7.12. Read online 2026-10-16; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Work in the universe containing $A,B,Z$. Put $X=\operatorname{Fun}(B,Z)$, $Y=\operatorname{Fun}(A,Z)$ and $f=u^*:X\to Y$. The definition node supplies the internal functor object, with its degreewise operators. By [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan], both $X$ and $Y$ are Kan; more generally $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)$ is Kan for every simplicial set $K$ in this universe.

Write $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}$ for vertices modulo edges as in [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence]. Its condition (i) is precisely the realization hypothesis of this item. For any simplicial parameter set $K$, take $W=\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)$, Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan]. Condition (ii) gives a bijection $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(B,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z))\to\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(A,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z))$ induced by $u$.

source.place: Corollary 3.6.4.3 (03X7), with Definition 3.1.7.12 (00UA) expanded in the cited node

proof.text: For $D=A$ or $D=B$, an $n$-simplex $F$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}(D,Z))$ is a map $K\times\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(D,Z)$. Define its uncurried map by $H_m(d,k,t)=F_m(k,t)_m(d,\mathrm{id}_{[m]})$. Conversely $H:D\times K\times\Delta^n\to Z$ defines $F_m(k,t)_r(d,\alpha)=H_r(d,K(\alpha)k,t\alpha)$ for every $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$. Simplicial naturality of $F$ shows that these constructions are inverse; the identity $H_s(D(\beta)d,K(\beta)k,t\beta)=Z(\beta)H_m(d,k,t)$ proves the required naturality of $H$. Restriction of $t$ along $[n']\to[n]$ commutes with both formulas. Exchanging the $D$ and $K$ coordinates gives the isomorphism with $\operatorname{Fun}(D,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z))$. Replacing $d=b$ by $u(a)$ in the displayed formula is exactly postcomposition by $f=u^*$ on $\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)$. Consequently step 2 gives a bijection $f_*:\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)\to\pi_0^{\mathrm e}\operatorname{Fun}(K,Y)$ for every $K$.

Use step 3 first with $K=Y$: surjectivity gives a representative $g:Y\to X$ whose class satisfies $[fg]=[\mathrm{id}_Y]$. Precomposing a path of edges of maps with $f$ gives $[fgf]=[f]$. Now use injectivity of step 3 with $K=X$: the two classes $[gf]$ and $[\mathrm{id}_X]$ have these equal images, so $[gf]=[\mathrm{id}_X]$. All brackets denote precisely the edge-generated equivalence relation; composing a representative edge with a fixed simplicial map preserves its endpoints, so the indicated precomposition is well defined.

The mapping sets $\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Y)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(X,X)$ are Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan], because $X,Y$ were proved Kan. In a Kan complex, every finite zigzag of edges compresses to one oriented edge: a degenerate edge gives reflexivity; given $a\to b$, fill the outer $\Lambda_0^2$ horn with edges $01=(a\to b)$ and $02=\mathrm{id}_a$ to obtain $b\to a$; given $a\to b\to c$, fill $\Lambda_1^2$ to obtain $a\to c$. Induction on the zigzag length applies these operations. Hence the two class equalities in step 4 give actual edges $fg\to\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $gf\to\mathrm{id}_X$. By the internal Fun definition these edges are maps $Y\times\Delta^1\to Y$ and $X\times\Delta^1\to X$ with exactly the required endpoint restrictions. They are the requested simplicial homotopies. Evaluating them at each vertex gives edge relations showing that $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}(g)$ is a two-sided inverse to $\pi_0^{\mathrm e}(f)$, proving the final bijection.
